sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: Compare a sphere of radius r and a cylinder of radius r and height 2r with two cones removed. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3 and centre O. A point P lies 5 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 4.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 3; the tangent length is 4.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 2.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 4.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 26. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 8. Write its equation.

choices: They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
